chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, and Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who breastfed a boy and a girl, he said: 'Another woman besides her [also breastfed them].' I said: 'No.' He said: 'The marriage prohibition is not established [as valid] unless there is another woman besides her [who also breastfed them].'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a single nursing event to establish a marriage prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the evidentiary standard for establishing permanent marriage prohibitions through fosterage (radāʿ), requiring proof that the nursing occurred with a woman other than the one in question to confirm the specific bond. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on verifying the exclusivity of the nursing relationship to prevent erroneous prohibitions, ensuring that the legal status of mahram is grounded in clear, distinct evidence rather than assumption.
